# India National Air Quality Index (CPCB)

Code `in_cpcb_naqi` · version 2014 (in force 2026) · scale: index 0–500 · method: continuous

## Sources

- [CPCB, About National Air Quality Index (categories and breakpoints for 8 pollutants)](https://cpcb.nic.in/displaypdf.php?id=bmF0aW9uYWwtYWlyLXF1YWxpdHktaW5kZXgvQWJvdXRfQVFJLnBkZg==), accessed 2026-10-21 (Wayback snapshot 2025-12-19; cpcb.nic.in unreachable)
- [CPCB, AQI-Calculator.xls (official calculator; formulas decoded from BIFF records)](https://cpcb.nic.in/upload/national-air-quality-index/AQI-Calculator.xls), accessed 2026-10-21 (Wayback snapshot 2023-08-05)

## Categories

| Level | Category | Index | Colour | Health message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Good | 0–50 | `#00B050` | Minimal impact. |
| 2 | Satisfactory | 51–100 | `#92D050` | Minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people. |
| 3 | Moderately polluted | 101–200 | `#FFFF00` | Breathing discomfort to people with lung or heart disease, children and older adults. |
| 4 | Poor | 201–300 | `#FF9900` | Breathing discomfort to people on prolonged exposure. |
| 5 | Very poor | 301–400 | `#FF0000` | Respiratory illness to people on prolonged exposure. |
| 6 | Severe | 401–500 | `#C00000` | Respiratory effects even on healthy people. |

## Breakpoints

| Pollutant | Averaging | Unit | Good | Satisfactory | Moderately polluted | Poor | Very poor | Severe |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PM10 | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–50 | 50–100 | 100–250 | 250–350 | 350–430 | > 430 |
| PM2.5 | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–30 | 30–60 | 60–90 | 90–120 | 120–250 | > 250 |
| NO₂ | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–40 | 40–80 | 80–180 | 180–280 | 280–400 | > 400 |
| SO₂ | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–40 | 40–80 | 80–380 | 380–800 | 800–1600 | > 1600 |
| NH₃ | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–200 | 200–400 | 400–800 | 800–1200 | 1200–1800 | > 1800 |
| Pb | 24h | µg/m³ | 0–0.5 | 0.5–1 | 1–2 | 2–3 | 3–3.5 | > 3.5 |
| CO | 8h_max24 | mg/m³ | 0–1 | 1–2 | 2–10 | 10–17 | 17–34 | > 34 |
| O₃ | 8h_max24 | µg/m³ | 0–50 | 50–100 | 100–168 | 168–208 | 208–748 | > 748 |

Index points at each breakpoint: 0, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400.

## Rules

- Sub-index is piecewise linear and continuous: each band runs from the previous band's upper breakpoint (e.g. PM2.5 30 to 60 maps to index 50 to 100). This matches the official calculator's formulas.
- Above the last breakpoint, the slope of the last band continues (e.g. PM2.5 > 250: 400 + (C - 250) x 100/130). The calculator does not cap at 500, so neither do we; the UI shows values above 500 as '500+'.
- AQI = max sub-index, published only when at least 3 pollutants are available and one of them is PM10 or PM2.5 (calculator note).
- 24-h averages for PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, NH3, Pb; maximum 8-h rolling mean within the trailing 24 h for CO and O3 ('max 8-hr' in the calculator).
- AQI is reported as an integer, rounded half-up.

## Implementation notes and source discrepancies

- Two official documents disagree. The 'About AQI' text says PM2.5 31 gives sub-index 51, which uses the EPA-style formula from the band's own lower bound. The calculator gives 51.67. We follow the calculator because it is the tool CPCB distributes for computation. The difference is at most 1 index point, at the start of a band.
- Calculator typo fixed: its O3 > 748 branch computes 400 + (C - 400) x 100/539, which jumps from 400 to 465 at 748. We use (C - 748). The calculator also divides by 539 for 208-748, a span of 540. We use 540, a difference of 0.2 index points at most.
- Minimum data completeness (16 of 24 hours, 6 of 8 hours) is our implementation choice. It follows CPCB's 2014 AQI report as quoted in secondary sources; we could not reach the primary report.
- Pb is part of the standard but no source in our regions reports it in real time.
